title: Proofs run without a network seal, and standing seal records stay as written
intention: The tester stops cutting a network namespace around proofs: every run, seal, reseal and hollow goes at isolation none under the always-on instance seal, a standing 'sealed' record is left as written until its proof next runs for its own reasons, and that run lands with the retirement as its stated reason.
why: Akien via peer akiendelllinux_cc_0 as F39, 2026-10-08, verbatim: "it sounds to me like we don't need it at all... this is deeper than i designed. what i said was everything needed to be able to be worked on live. self testing, self checking... as long as things are working, we don't need to retest 400 proofs for something i never thought we needed." Measured 2026-10-08: the namespace's only recorded why (isolation.py:15-20, the 2026-07-13 incident) is the single inference slot, which moves to its owner in child d0672a46aa7e; meanwhile the seal costs every hollow run inside the verdict sandbox an exit 2 (c54d744aa9ac, worked around on 3d31d968a1a0 and 46ece5fd9f69). Folds the trouble at /home/akien/.cairn/logs/tester/0/20261008.190915.381284.TesterDevice.raise_trouble.json (F38), superseded by this ruling.
traces_to: RULE 1 (the tester stops enforcing a rule about inference_domain's resource); Law 4 (the slot rule moves to physics at its owner, d0672a46aa7e, binding every caller rather than proofs only); Law 9 + Akien's ruling (no mass re-run — a standing seal is not made red by a retirement); CP4 (the seal's cost serves no current consumer).
how: cairn/devices/tester: (1) isolation.py — NetnsIsolation is removed; get_isolation('netns'|'seal') raises ValueError naming the retirement (constant NETWORK_SEAL_RETIRED, which names this ticket and the ruling); the module docstring says the network seal is retired and why, and the instance seal is untouched. (2) cli.py — isolation_for returns 'none' for every run; --netns stays defined but refuses with exit 2 naming the retirement before any proof runs; the OVERRIDE print and the isolation_for_seal import go. (3) reseal.py:437 — iso = isolation or 'none'. (4) hollow.py — seal_isolation returns 'none'. (5) device.py:788 and reseal.py:501/558 pass unsealing_because=NETWORK_SEAL_RETIRED to persist_validation, which the store's own guard (validation_store.py:746-758) writes into evidence only when a measured seal meets an open reading — so a standing sealed record changes only when its own proof next lands, and says why. (6) The charter's 'owns the network' text is restated through the artifact door. validation_store is not changed (isolation_for_seal stays the store's vocabulary; the tester stops calling it). Proof changes are question open-41bc11343280.
falsifier: Falsifier: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_network_seal_is_retired.py under PROVES {'d80360545e91': {'1','2','3','4'}}: (1) `cairn test --seal` over a fixture proof whose standing record reads sealed runs at isolation none (no --unshare-net in the sandbox argv) and lands green with evidence.unsealing_because naming the retirement, no SealDowngradeRefused, and a sibling fixture validation's bytes unchanged; (2) the reseal door over the same fixture lands green the same way; (3) hollow.seal_isolation reads 'none' for a sealed proof, and a hollow started inside an instance sandbox measures instead of refusing with SealUnavailable; (4) `cairn test --netns` exits 2 naming the retirement and runs nothing, and get_isolation('netns') raises naming it. Every instance-seal tooth (test_instance_seal.py, test_a_seal_inside_a_seal_inherits.py teeth 2-3) stays green. Hollow: reverting cli.py/device.py reds 1 and 4, reseal.py reds 2, hollow.py reds 3, isolation.py reds 4. Horizon: the next PROVED crossing whose hollow criterion is `bin/cairn test --hollow <id>` runs it inside the verdict sandbox with exit 0 (c54d744aa9ac's exit 2 gone). Wrong intent if: a proof's correctness is found to depend on the network being absent, or any standing validation other than the one being run is rewritten by a run.
watchme: none, because the corpus reading is the existing probe /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/devices/tester/probes/seal_measurements_are_not_dropped.py, which this ticket re-points (question open-41bc11343280 (e)) to count a record carrying the retirement as the standing reason rather than an escape
